brief: GS has consolidated its multi-asset view as rising yields and energy prices offset earnings tailwinds since summer, hitting rate-sensitive equities, credit spreads and Euro sovereign spreads. It shifts back to overweight equities for 3 months (in line with 12 months) on resilient earnings and improved valuation asymmetry after the de-rating, favoring a barbell of AI beneficiaries and rate-sensitive, high-dividend, low-volatility names. It shifts to overweight bonds for 12 months (neutral for 3 months) because inflation normalization and a less hawkish policy path should let 10-year yields move from a portfolio headwind to a hedge, while preferring cash and short duration near term given midterm-election and Middle East uncertainty. Credit stays underweight on tight spreads relative to all-in yields and supply/releveraging risk. Its Risk Appetite Indicator's monetary-policy component has fallen to one of its lowest levels since 2000, a pattern that historically preceded equity recoveries except in 2022. With implied volatility anchored, GS recommends VIX call spreads, front-end receiver swaptions and FX hedges against Euro sovereign stress (led by French spread widening) as inexpensive protection.
